quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: During a normal turn, what should the motorcycle and rider do?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, both the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider sits upright.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals when you plan to change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on a road with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake immediately.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear tire locks on a road with good traction, leave it locked until you stop completely. You can still control the motorcycle as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, they are required.
No, but they are recommended.
No, they are not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is true about low-speed motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They can be fatal.
They are never serious.
They rarely cause injuries.
They happen often, so they are not a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be deadly.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing where to position your motorcycle in a lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which lane position makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles from that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that allows other drivers to see you and gives you enough space to react safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right, so be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, what should you do?

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road first to learn how your motorcycle handles with a passenger or heavy load before riding in traffic.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover the ankle
A snug baseball cap
Gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: A snug baseball cap
questions.explanation: Proper protection includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a strong jacket and long pants, high ankle-covering boots, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to acceleration and stopping time?

options.text: Faster acceleration, but slower stopping.
Slower acceleration and slower stopping.
Slower acceleration, but faster stopping.
Faster acceleration and faster stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower acceleration and slower stopping.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes a motorcycle take longer to speed up and longer to stop.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them to do?

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.
Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as comfortable without crowding you.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine but still be underinflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?

options.text: Dry pavement
Gravel
Snow
Leaves

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, paint markings, and metal plates all reduce traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two people.
Only one set of footrests.
No need for protective clothing on the passenger.
A sticker on the brake light warning of a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two people.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat made for two riders. It should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear recommended for riders.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, how should you position your body?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean opposite to the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with the motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans to counterbalance it.

questions.question: When it starts raining, where should you ride?

options.text: Get off the road.
In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track often works best, but it depends on traffic conditions.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything you need to see.
Use mirrors and turn your head to check blind spots.
Signal and move immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use mirrors and turn your head to check blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for best protection.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time needed to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you easiest.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you easiest.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Do not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
Do not allow them to ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to understand how to stay safe. Always give them complete instructions before the ride, even if they have ridden before.

questions.question: When should you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When there is not enough room on the other side for you to completely cross.
When you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough room on the other side for you to completely cross.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your motorcycle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Behind the rear axle.
On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them properly or use saddlebags. High loads change your motorcycle's balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it fits snugly.
If it is free of defects.
If it has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet must be certified by the DOT, fit snugly, and be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps to protect you properly.

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger do?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Never ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because your hands will get too hot.
They provide a better grip on the handgrips and protect your hands.
You should not wear them because they make the controls harder to use.
You should only wear them on cooler days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a better grip on the handgrips and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Leather gloves or other durable gloves improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: What are the four steps to safely complete a turn?

options.text: Slow, look, lean, and roll.
Slow, shift, look, and lurch.
Press, lean, turn, and grip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow, look, lean, and roll.
questions.explanation: To safely turn, slow down as you approach the turn. Look through the turn to where you want to go. Press the handlebar in the direction of the turn to lean the bike. Roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them NOT to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unless necessary. This helps you stay focused on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you brake.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group is less easily separated in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be difficult to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less easily separated in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them more safely. They are less likely to get separated by traffic or traffic lights. Slower riders do not have to rush to catch up.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?

options.text: Better riding abilities.
Slowed bodily functions.
More nervousness.
More alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed bodily functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs warn you that you are in or approaching a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children and follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until it is clear and safe to pass through the intersection.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist adjust their following distance?

options.text: Always keep it the same.
Change it based on riding conditions.
It is not necessary in most situations.
Avoid it to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change it based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Also increase it on slippery pavement, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.
